text: The verdict is the keep rule's three bounds checked in order (coverage>=90, agreement>=95, Pi p95<=1.5x CLI); adopt needs all three. The number is round1(106/111*100)=95.5 and one more disagreement gives 94.6, so the verdict holds on a one-row margin.

Every headline metric reproduces from the recorded calls: 106/111 agreement, median_abs_dp exactly 0.0100 over 1689 order-key differences, p50/p95 249/340 pi vs 326/387 cli, coverage total with excluded=0 unmeasured=0 timeouts=0.

All five disagreements sit inside the 12 rows with either side's top-2 mean margin under 0.10; the other 99 rows agree 100 pct. Three of the five flip on a mean gap under 0.07 on at least one side (rr-iter3-071, rr-iter3-081, rr-iter3-125).

Agreement is a mean-of-orders construct: per-order top-key agreement is 317/333=95.2 pct vs the row-level 95.5 pct; mean and 2-of-3 majority select the same 106 rows. rr-iter3-127 has identical order picks on all three orders yet counts as a disagreement because averaged means cross by 0.023 vs 0.010.

rr-iter3-125's CLI top key is an exact tie (system-deep-loop and none both 0.3166667) settled by submitted option order; none is appended last so it can only win strictly. The 037 record's shorthand that the CLI picked none is the tie's losing side.
Rotation sensitivity is present on both sides: 9 of 111 pi rows and 12 of 111 cli rows split their top key across the three cyclic orders.

The cost figure is not reproducible from the run's records: cost_per_100 is mean(usage.cost.total)*100 but the Pi call records store no usage field, so 0.0022 lives only in report.json and the session's in-process numbers.
Pi's latency win is consistent but modest: mean 260 vs 332 ms, p50 249 vs 326, p95 340 vs 387 (ratio 0.878 vs the 1.5 bound); the full live run was 333 calls in about 1 min 29 s.

The two sides asked the same nominal model through different providers (openrouter typesafe/jev-1.13 vs official jev-1.13.0), so 95.5 pct is cross-provider agreement of one model family and the flips are backend/provider effects.
The latency pair is not same-day: Pi fresh 2026-09-30 vs CLI recorded 2026-09-29; the --pi --cli both-sides path exists and has never run.

state_sha12 (sha256(state).slice(0,12)) travels with every Pi call as the only in-record proof of what was sent; CLI records carry advisor_ms/child_wall_ms/health_ms instead, so the two recorded call shapes are asymmetric.
